adapt_rules_reviews_snacs.txt:
Useful rules from SNACS guidelines + purchased review examples:

1) Motion/event endpoint to institution/business names:
- With verbs of going/coming, 'to' before a school/business can take function p.Goal while the scene role reflects the destination as an organization: p.Org/p.Goal.
- Example: 'Went to the school' -> school is construed as organizational destination, not plain p.Locus.

2) Partitives with 'of':
- In quantificational expressions like 'each of you', annotate 'of' as p.QuantityItem/p.Whole.
- The subset/selected item is the role; the larger set is the function.

3) Emotional adjective + 'of' stimulus/topic:
- With adjectives such as 'proud of', the complement can be the stimulus for the emotion while 'of' lexically marks topic-like relation: p.Stimulus/p.Topic.
- Do not default all adjective+'of' complements to p.Topic/p.Topic.

4) Possessive determiners are not uniform:
- Possessive determiner before an event/result noun can indicate the semantic participant associated with that noun rather than ownership.
- Example: 'your massive contributions' -> 'your' = contributor, so p.Agent/p.Gestalt.
- Concrete ownership with ordinary possessed nouns stays p.Possessor/p.Possessor.
- Example: 'your money' -> p.Possessor/p.Possessor.

5) Temporal span 'throughout':
- 'throughout the year' is p.Duration/p.Duration when it denotes an extended span over which something holds.

6) Means marker 'by':
- In expressions like 'start out by saying', 'by' introducing the action used to accomplish another action is p.Means/p.Means.

7) Business/location names with 'at' and street names with 'on':
- Static location at establishments: 'at Lovely Nails' -> p.Locus/p.Locus.
- Street-address relation with 'on' + road/street name is also p.Locus/p.Locus.

General exception reminder from guidelines:
- Scene role and lexical function may differ when the governing predicate imposes one relation but the adposition lexically contributes another.
- For possessives/genitives, choose labels from semantic relation of possessor to head noun; ownership is only one subtype and may shift to Agent, Gestalt, etc.
